# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Age:** Elderly, over 50 years old  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P14](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0014)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- **Status:** Widow  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** Chaperone and housekeeper  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>; Aunty  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Jamesina is a tiny old woman with a softly triangular, pink-cheeked face, snow-white hair worn in quaint puffs over her ears, and large, soft blue eyes filled with youth. She dresses in an old-fashioned style, occasionally wearing a fluffy white shawl over her shoulders. Her hands are nimble and constantly engaged in knitting.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c32 P15](../source/v03-c32.md#nw-v03-c32-p0015)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina is a sweet, cheerful, and indulgent woman who keeps a youthful heart and an optimistic philosophy. She possesses a dry, mischievous sense of humor and candidly admits her own old-fashioned views without imposing them strictly on others. Possessing a great love for cats, she is a deeply loving, motherly figure who value genuine affection above mere propriety.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P15](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0015), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P61](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0061)_

- Indulgent and youth-hearted  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

## Abilities

- Knitting  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>
- Housekeeping  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>

## Goals

- To provide a happy, comfortable home for her student charges at Patty's Place  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c18 P1](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0001)</sub>

## History

Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, who died at sea before she was born. After her own daughter married and departed for missionary work in India, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house until Stella Maynard invited her to act as matron and housekeeper for a group of Redmond College students. She moved into Patty's Place in Kingsport alongside Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon, bringing along her cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat. Over the next two college years, she provided a warm, motherly atmosphere, managing the household, indulging the girls, and adopting a stray cat named Rusty into the family fold. During the holiday seasons she remained behind to look after Patty's Place and the pets. Later, when Anne's firstborn child died, Aunt Jamesina's continued presence and love remained a comfort to the girls as they completed their studies and graduated.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P48](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0048), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P61](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0061), [v3 c18 P1](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0001), [v3 c35 P0](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0000)_

## Background by volume

- Named Jamesina after her father James, who was drowned at sea before her birth  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- Her only daughter married and went to India as a foreign missionary  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025)</sub>
- Inherited two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, whom she cares for deeply  <sub>[v3 c16 P55](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0055), [v3 c16 P59](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0059)</sub>

## Quotes

> Do your duty by God and your neighbor and yourself, and have a good time. That’s my philosophy and it’s always worked pretty well.  <sub>[v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004)</sub>

> I’ve a notion that such prayers don’t rise very far. I used to pray that I might be enabled to forgive a certain person, but I know now I really didn’t want to forgive her. When I finally got that I did want to I forgave her without having to pray about it.  <sub>[v3 c35 P15](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0015)</sub>

> When you’ve learned to laugh at the things that should be laughed at, and not to laugh at those that shouldn’t, you’ve got wisdom and understanding.  <sub>[v3 c37 P19](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0019)</sub>

> People who haven’t natural gumption never learn, neither in college nor life. If they live to be a hundred they really don’t know anything more than when they were born.  <sub>[v3 c37 P26](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0026)</sub>
